config.title: Counter App

intro.title: Counter App
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a simple counter application that displays a number and has buttons to increment and decrement that value. This project introduces you to Angular components, which are the building blocks of Angular applications that encapsulate both the visual template and the logic that controls it. You'll learn how to manage component state using properties, handle user interactions through event binding, and update the user interface dynamically using Angular's data binding features. The counter app demonstrates fundamental concepts like component lifecycle, property binding, and event handling that form the foundation for building more complex Angular applications. By the end of this lesson, you'll understand how Angular components work together to create interactive web applications.
intro.usecase: Counter patterns are fundamental building blocks in modern web applications, appearing in shopping cart quantity selectors, social media like/dislike buttons, and pagination controls. E-commerce platforms use counters for inventory tracking, vote tallies in polling applications, and notification badges that display unread message counts. Developers implement counter logic in dashboard widgets showing metrics, form input steppers for numeric values, and interactive features like rating systems where users increment scores.

objectives: Initialize component state to store a numeric counter value
Implement methods to increment and decrement counter values
Bind click events to buttons for counter manipulation
Render dynamic counter values in the component template
Configure property binding to display real-time state changes
Construct a functional Angular component with interactive controls
Apply TypeScript typing to counter state and methods

steps.title: Import Angular Component decorator
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the Component decorator that you'll need to create Angular components.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: importing a decorator
import { Injectable } from '@angular/core';
steps.expectedOutcome: The Component decorator is imported and available for use in creating Angular components.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you're importing Component specifically from '@angular/core' using the correct syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: use the import statement with curly braces to import the Component decorator from '@angular/core'.

steps.title: Create the CounterApp component class
steps.instruction: Create and export a class named CounterApp decorated with the @Component decorator.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator above a class declaration. The class should be exported so it can be used in other parts of the application.
steps.seedCode:
import { Component } from '@angular/core';

// Create and export the CounterApp component class here
steps.expectedOutcome: A CounterApp class is created with the @Component decorator and exported for use in the application.
successCriteria: The CounterApp class is decorated with @Component and exported.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your class is named CounterApp, has the @Component decorator, and is exported.
steps.feedbackWrong: create a class named CounterApp, add the @Component decorator above it, and export the class.

steps.title: Initialize the counter state property
steps.instruction: Add a counter property initialized to 0 inside the CounterApp component class
steps.hint: In Angular, component properties are declared directly inside the class. Use the syntax: propertyName = initialValue;
steps.expectedOutcome: The CounterApp component class will have a counter property set to 0
successCriteria: A counter property is declared and initialized to 0 inside the CounterApp class
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure the counter property is initialized to 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: The counter property should be declared inside the class with an initial value of 0.

steps.title: Define the increment method
steps.instruction: Add an increment method to the CounterApp class that increases the counter property by 1
steps.hint: Create a method inside the class that adds 1 to the current counter value
steps.expectedOutcome: The CounterApp class will have an increment method that adds 1 to the counter property
successCriteria: An increment method is defined in the CounterApp class that increases the counter property by 1
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure the method increases the counter property by exactly 1.
steps.feedbackWrong: The increment method should be inside the CounterApp class and should add 1 to the counter property.

steps.title: Define the decrement method
steps.instruction: Add a decrement method to the CounterApp component that decreases the counter property by 1
steps.hint: Create a method similar to increment, but subtract 1 from this.counter instead of adding 1
steps.expectedOutcome: The CounterApp component will have a decrement method that reduces the counter value by 1
successCriteria: A decrement method is defined that decreases this.counter by 1
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your decrement method decreases this.counter by 1 (using this.counter-- or this.counter -= 1).
steps.feedbackWrong: The decrement method should decrease the counter property by 1. Use this.counter-- or this.counter -= 1 inside the method.

steps.title: Define the reset method
steps.instruction: Add a reset method to the CounterApp class that sets the counter property back to 0.
steps.hint: Create a method called reset that assigns 0 to this.counter, similar to how increment modifies the counter.
steps.expectedOutcome: The CounterApp class will have a reset method that sets the counter property to 0.
successCriteria: A reset method is defined that assigns 0 to this.counter
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your reset method sets this.counter to 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: The reset method should set this.counter = 0 to reset the counter value.

steps.title: Add the component template structure
steps.instruction: Add a @Component decorator above the CounterApp class with a template property containing a div wrapper and an h1 heading that says 'Counter App'.
steps.hint: The @Component decorator needs a template property with HTML. Use template literals (backticks) for multiline templates.
steps.expectedOutcome: The CounterApp class will have a @Component decorator with a template containing a div wrapper and an h1 heading.
successCriteria: @Component decorator is added above the class with a template property containing a div and h1 with 'Counter App' text.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure the @Component decorator includes a template property with both a div wrapper and an h1 heading.
steps.feedbackWrong: The @Component decorator should be placed above the class declaration and include a template property with HTML containing a div and h1 element.

steps.title: Display the counter value
steps.instruction: Add a paragraph element that displays the current counter value using Angular interpolation syntax.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} around the property name to display its value in the template.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: displaying a property value

Current score: {{ score }}
steps.expectedOutcome: A paragraph element displays the current counter value using Angular interpolation, showing the numeric value of the counter property.
successCriteria: A paragraph element is added to the template that uses interpolation syntax {{ counter }} to display the counter value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you're using the correct interpolation syntax with double curly braces around the counter property name.
steps.feedbackWrong: add a paragraph element inside the template and use Angular's interpolation syntax {{ }} with the counter property name inside.

steps.title: Add increment and decrement buttons
steps.instruction: Add two buttons below the paragraph: one labeled 'Increment' that calls the increment method on click, and one labeled 'Decrement' that calls the decrement method on click.
steps.hint: Use the (click) event binding syntax to connect button clicks to your component methods.
steps.expectedOutcome: Two buttons are added to the template, one for incrementing and one for decrementing the counter, with proper click event bindings.
successCriteria: Two buttons are present with labels 'Increment' and 'Decrement', and they have (click) event bindings to the increment() and decrement() methods respectively.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good progress! Make sure you have both buttons with the correct labels and click handlers.
steps.feedbackWrong: add two buttons with (click) event bindings that call the increment() and decrement() methods.

steps.title: Add reset button
steps.instruction: Add a reset button with (click) event binding to the reset method in the template below the increment and decrement buttons.
steps.hint: Add a third button element with the text 'Reset' and bind the (click) event to the reset method using (click)="reset()".
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: button with click event binding
<button (click)="clearData()">Clear</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will have a reset button that calls the reset method when clicked, completing the counter functionality.
successCriteria: A reset button is added with (click) event binding to the reset method
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure the reset button has the (click) event binding to call the reset method.
steps.feedbackWrong: add a button element with (click)="reset()" event binding. The button should be placed in the template alongside the other buttons.
